A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same latent recalibration work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching material that was moved or renumbered.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices H–J report original recalibration experiments on 29 tabular datasets and AFHQ, including alternative flow architectures and deliberately undertrained models.

after.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original benchmark results, supplemented by flow-matching experiments, decision utilities, calibration timings and synthetic score-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The central LR radial transformation, calibration-map estimation and predictive-density calculation remain unchanged. Appendix E.2 adds a limited methodological extension: Algorithm 1 generalizes density-based HDR-R to recalibration using an arbitrary pre-rank function. Applying LR to flow matching does not introduce different LR steps.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained tabular regression and AFHQ coverage, Appendix F introduces a utility-maximizing concrete-allocation task on SLUMP, and Appendix J.2 reports CIFAR-10 calibration timings. Conversely, v1's noiseless AFHQ scenario is removed. These changes materially alter task and test-scenario coverage; flow matching itself is an added model setting.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain the unrecalibrated BASE predictor and HDR-R, with BASE alone in the AFHQ comparison. New experiments reuse these methods. HDR-R was already evaluated in v1's tables despite incomplete main-figure legends; the generalized pre-rank algorithm is not evaluated as an additional competitor.

E3.justification: Fixed convex-potential-flow and MAF configurations in v1 are replaced by validation-NLL grid searches over architecture and learning rate in v2 Appendices E and K. New protocols include flow-matching configurations and a decision experiment comparing 125 Monte Carlo samples with 5×5×5 numerical integration. The main data splits and appendix metric formulas remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix J adds analyses decomposing NLL gains, measuring calibration efficiency, and varying an oracle predictor's spread to investigate NLL versus energy-score discrimination. These address previously untested mechanism and evaluation questions. The earlier reliability diagrams, predictive-density examples and two-epoch misspecification experiment are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The main ten-split experiments, twenty AFHQ evaluations, standard-error reporting, 90% consistency bands and Z-test convention are retained. The new synthetic analysis explicitly contrasts estimates from 10 and 5,000 runs with standard errors in Tables 8–9. This adds a localized replication study, not increased replication of the existing benchmarks.

E6.justification: Convex-potential-flow and MAF result tables are extensively revised under changed model-selection settings. For example, SLU BASE/LR NLL changes from 5.40/2.16 in v1 Table 4 to 2.61/2.29 in v2 Table 10; this is not a same-setting performance comparison. New utility, timing, diagnostic and flow-matching results are added, while noiseless AFHQ results disappear. The misspecified-model tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The latent-calibration definition, Proposition 1, finite-sample guarantee, conformal and quantile-recalibration relationships, and radial-Jacobian proof are retained. V2 adds supporting inverse-map derivations in Appendix I and explicit calibration/inference complexity arguments in J.2. These extend the mathematical analysis without changing the central calibration guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the stated applicability from conditional normalizing flows to invertible generative models, explicitly including flow matching. The central contributions—latent calibration, an explicit recalibrated density, finite-sample guarantees and improved empirical calibration—remain the same.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations attributing NLL gains to more plausible latent codes and weak energy-score changes to limited discrimination. It specifies inability to correct latent directions, incompatibility with VAEs/DDPMs, and a discrete-output warning based on BLO. It also interprets decision-utility results, while dropping v1's explicit concluding limitation concerning calibration-set size and density-estimation quality.

D1.justification: V2 supplies HDR-R pseudocode, substantially fuller base-predictor construction and likelihood-computation details, and explicit hyperparameter-search grids for convex potential flows, MAFs and flow matching. The decision experiment documents requirement regions, utilities and numerical-estimation budgets. These materially expand reproducibility information; the code-access link and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New citations support flow matching and neural ODEs, input-convex networks, VAE/diffusion applicability boundaries, scoring-rule discrimination and anomaly detection. The principal positioning against HDR-R, quantile recalibration and conformal prediction, including most extended related work, remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and calibration background are extensively edited, and distribution/CDF/PDF notation is standardized throughout. The appendices are reorganized: reliability diagrams move, base-predictor exposition gains a separate section, and full results become part of a broader analysis section. This constitutes substantial editorial restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adds decision, NLL-decomposition, timing, score-sensitivity and flow-matching tables, two flow-matching figures, and an algorithm display. Existing plots receive legend/axis revisions, the two-part AFHQ table becomes a single table, and retained figures and result tables are relocated and reflowed. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: Flow-matching tests, measured calibration times, validation-based tuning and more specific limitations strengthen support for applicability and efficiency beyond v1. However, unreconciled NLL values between v2 Tables 5 and 10 weaken the new mechanism analysis, and the decision experiment's claim of PDF necessity exceeds its fixed-budget comparison. Removing the noiseless AFHQ test also loses useful evidence. The additions therefore support a limited net improvement.
